blocks.text: LESSON 13
THE JUDGMENT
Scripture Texts: Ecclesiastes 12:13-14; Romans 2:16; John 12:48; Matthew 16:27; Romans 2:7-11; 2 Thessalonians 1:6-10; Romans 8:19-23

As people work fervently here in this life to earn an earthly living, payday is looked forward to with great expectation. It is the reward for our labors. The same applies to the Christian who labors and fights for the cause of Christ through his days appointed here in this life. Death is his reward, his final crown of victory over Satan and the power of evil.
This is the day of all days, the day he leaves all the battles behind with their troubles and sorrows, and goes to be with Jesus in Heaven for all eternity—PAYDAY.
MEMORY VERSE: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. —Romans 6:23
Importance of Our Response

We have been studying how God, through Jesus Christ, has given pro-vision for each soul to live righteously. How each of us use these basic pro-visions determines our success or failure in this life. Our response to what God has provided determines what our payday will bring—life everlasting in Heaven or death in hell. We must look to the Heavenly goal as the only thing of worth.
The Day of Judgment

Ecclesiastes 12:13-14 The Bible, both the Old and New Testaments, clearly teaches there is to be a Judgment Day, a day when all men and wom-en shall receive their just dues (Acts 10:42; Revelation 20:12-13). We shall all be judged according to the Gospel of Christ. The Judge is appointed by God, and His jurisdiction includes the whole earth (Acts 17:31). Both living and dead are included in the Judgment. Christ is that Judge (Romans 14:10).

Romans 2:16 A standard is fixed by which we shall be judged—the stan-dard under which each lived. No one having lived under the dispensation of grace and truth will be judged by the Law, only those living under the Law will be judged by the Law.

The Judgment does not determine whether or not the individual is guilty. This fact will be fully settled at death. The man or woman dying in sin will remain guilty forever. The fact that all receive a reward at death proves this. The Judgment will lack investigation because to God all things are fully known. "Every knee shall bow . . . and every tongue shall confess" (Romans 14:11) without forced acknowledgment.

John 12:48 The revealed will of God is the standard of judgment. Christ told His hearers they would be judged by His words. Judgment will depend on the degree of knowledge of the individual, not only on what he knows, but on what he had an opportunity to know and neglected to learn. Some have a more complete understanding of God's will than others, so are more respon-sible. The standards by which men are to be judged are the same as the standards by which sin is now imputed. The Judgment will be perfectly just. There will be no spite, but only justice.
The Day of Reward
Matthew 16:27 The same reasons that call for a Judgment require that the Judgment be accompanied with suitable rewards. The Bible teaches fu-ture and final rewards for all.

Romans 2:7-11 The rewards are not received on this earth. The earth is a place of probation, a preparation place for the eternal state. Change and decay are evident everywhere. This earth is not a suitable place for eternal existence. The earth will be destroyed at the Day of Judgment, so it cannot be the eternal home of either the righteous or the wicked.

2 Thessalonians 1:6-7 Heaven is a prepared place where Christ sits at the Father's right hand awaiting the reception of the saints. He will come for us and take us to that place where He now is. Heaven will not be this earth made over. Heaven is a real place to which Christ ascended and from which He will return.

2 Thessalonians 1:8-10 The wicked will be punished in hell. As Heaven is a prepared place, so is hell. Hell is not the grave. The grave is not a place of punishment, but a place to which all go regardless of character. It is only the body that enters the grave. Hell is a place and not a mere condition (Psalm 9:17), and man, "both soul and body"(Matthew 10:28), may be sent there. The wicked shall be in a state of conscious suffering in hell. This is described as "weeping and gnashing of teeth" (Matthew 8:12), and a place of unquenchable fire. The rich man in hell had all his senses.
The Nature of Rewards

Romans 8:19-23 Paul here, considering only saved people, pictured God's children as delivered from the bondage of corruption—freed from sorrow, pain, and death. No temptation or danger of falling will be there.

Whole creation—all people, even those which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan. Waiting for the adoption . . . for the redemption of our body—to have our flesh redeemed from sickness and death, given life with Christ forever. "Our vile body" will "be fashioned like unto his glorious body" (Philippians 3:21). "An inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you" (1 Peter 1:4). "And they shall reign for ever and ever" (Revelation 22:5).

Our bodies will be in Heaven, just like Jesus' risen body. He had flesh and bones; He could handle things; He ate; He talked; He could hear. He had all five senses. Oh, how wonderful meeting the saints of all ages! DO NOT MISS IT.
JUST A THOUGHT
Every person is a soldier of Jesus Christ or an agent for the devil.

Christ is that Judge (Romans 14:10).
Romans 2:16 A standard is fixed by which we shall be judged—the stan-dard under which each lived.
No one having lived under the dispensation of grace and truth will be judged by the Law, only those living under the Law will be judged by the Law.
The Judgment does not determine whether or not the individual is guilty.
This fact will be fully settled at death.
The man or woman dying in sin will remain guilty forever.

Judgment will depend on the degree of knowledge of the individual, not only on what he knows, but on what he had an opportunity to know and neglected to learn.

The standards by which men are to be judged are the same as the standards by which sin is now imputed.

The rich man in hell had all his senses.
Romans 8:19-23 Paul here, considering only saved people, pictured God's children as delivered from the bondage of corruption—freed from sorrow, pain, and death.
No temptation or danger of falling will be there.
Whole creation—all people, even those which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan.

Waiting for the adoption . . . for the redemption of our body—to have our flesh redeemed from sickness and death, given life with Christ forever. "Our vile body" will "be fashioned like unto his glorious body" (Philippians 3:21). "An inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you" (1 Peter 1:4). "And they shall reign for ever and ever" (Revelation 22:5).
Our bodies will be in Heaven, just like Jesus' risen body.
He had flesh and bones; He could handle things; He ate; He talked; He could hear.

Oh, how wonderful meeting the saints of all ages!

lines.text: CHURCH OF GOD
SUNDAY SCHOOL QUARTERLY
CHRISTIAN WARFARE
CHRISTIAN WARFARE
CONTENTS
Strangers and Pilgrims on the Earth . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 31
NOTE TO THE TEACHERS
This booklet is intended to be a help in preparing Sunday school les-
sons. The title, subject, and topics are only the menu. It is your respon-
sibility to prepare the meal.
The proper ingredients are the salty inspirations of the Holy Spirit,
seasoned with His grace. Bake the ingredients at a hot temperature in the
oven of prayer. The time-tested recipe for preparing a nutritious meal is
found in 2 Timothy 2:15, "Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a
workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of
truth."
LESSON 1
COMMANDER IN CHIEF
Scripture Texts: Ephesians 1:20-23; John 14:1-6; Hebrews 1:8; 9:24-28
Did you ever wonder why there is so much spiritual defeat among the
people today? It is because man without God is nothing. This series of
lessons is arranged in hope of helping to prepare a people for the hardship of
Christian warfare. We hope to cause people to see who our enemy really is,
the weapons he uses, and what we must do to prepare for victory over this
enemy.
MEMORY VERSE: The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into
his hand.
—John 3:35
Jesus, the Sure Rock
God has given His Son all power (Matthew 28:18). As Commander in
Chief of His army, He calls, recruits, chooses, prepares, trains, sends, sup-
plies, empowers, motivates, directs, and leads us. It is all Christ. We are only
tools for Him to use.
Ephesians 1:20-23 We cannot have confidence without something to
place confidence in. We cannot be courageous without a foundation to rest
courage upon. There must be something to trust. Without a source of
strength, courage is an empty boast that fails. In Jesus Christ, a saint has a
foundation rock for confidence. Living in Him, we can have assurance even
in the midst of trials, discouragements, and persecutions. He is the Rock
from which we draw our strength (1 Corinthians 10:4), the Rock upon which
the church is built (Matthew 16:18), the Rock of our salvation (Psalm
89:26), the Rock who is a "stumbling stone" and "offence" to rebellious sin-
ners but a mighty bulwark to believers (Romans 9:33), and the Rock upon
which we can build and be safe in the storm (Matthew 7:24-25). Friend,
anchor now in Jesus, and you can say when the storm strikes, "But the L ORD
is my defence; and my God is the rock of my refuge" (Psalm 94:22).
Jesus, the Only Leader
When Jesus was on earth He wrote that the whole world was "in wicked-
ness" (1 John 5:19). A look around in our time shows that it has not changed.
It appears to be sinking deeper and deeper into sin. Second Timothy 3:13
warns that "evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and
being deceived."
Evil forces are crowding in upon us. Communism is moving ever nearer
as it grasps one area after another. The National and World Councils of
Churches, influenced by modernism and humanism, are working for a "one
world church" to dominate the field of religion. Roman Catholicism is
attempting to draw the Protestant denominations into her ecumenical union.
Moves are being made and laws passed to cut off tax exemptions to
Christians and church property. We cannot tell when great opposition and
persecution may be brought upon us as it has been to Christians of other
ages. We may be called upon, as others have before us, to defend our faith
in Christ and perhaps seal it with our blood.
If this comes, will we be ready? Will we be good soldiers prepared to
fight a good fight of faith? If so, we must have our faith anchored in the
Rock, Christ Jesus, so that the storm of the enemy cannot shake it.
This is no time for fear and despair, but rather for deepened faith and
determination. It is time to establish and strengthen our contact with God,
our consecration to Him, and our closeness with Him. Never forget that God
has given our Leader, Jesus Christ, all power.
Jesus Christ Has the Preeminence
John 14:6 Jesus saith . . . I am the way—the way to the Father's house,
to Heaven, to union with God—the truth—enlightening dark places, reveal-
ing true knowledge, answering all questions—and the life—giving fullness
of life to the dead soul, giving it His life, making that life continue forever.
Jesus is the only way. There is no other. No man cometh unto the Father,
but by me. Not by parent, preacher, priest, saint, angel, Mary, or good
works. Heeding this, we are saved the despair of a fruitless search down a
wrong way.
Jesus Is God, King, and High Priest
Hebrews 1:8 God is speaking to His only Son, Jesus. Thy throne, O
God—Jesus is the "KING OF KINGS" (Revelation 19:16). He is deity. This
is important to settle in our minds. We must know in Whom we are trusting
and that His strength is sufficient for all our needs, or we cannot put full
faith in Him. Is for ever and ever—eternal, never to end—a sceptre of
righteousness—Christ's rule is righteous; He uses justice, mercy, and love.
Hebrews 9:24-28 Christ is the High Priest—the One who is able to repre-
sent man before God, to offer sacrifices for man to God, and to draw nigh to
God on man's behalf. He made atonement for sin. Christ is the true antitype
of the high priests of the Law. Christ did His work once for all. He made
atonement for sin.
The high priests of the Law were purely human. They offered the blood
of animals in a man-built holy place. They repeated the offering every year
because it was insufficient to cover the need permanently. Christ is the ful-
fillment. He is the divine High Priest Who offered Himself in the presence
of God just once because His offering was fully sufficient to put away sin.
Christ is dependable as a Savior. His remedy for sin is certain—as certain
as death and judgment. Everything He does is perfect. He is worthy of our
faith and trust.
If we are to successfully meet the hard things of life and the opposition
of Satan, the very first requirement is a Savior Who can save. Do you have
Him?
JUST A THOUGHT
This life is a school of EDUCATION.
Each day brings forth a RECITATION.
Death ends the term without VACATION,
and then comes the final EXAMINATION.
LESSON 2
THE ARTICLES OF WAR
Scripture Texts: Jude 3; Hebrews 6:17-20; 7:19; 1 Corinthians 15:22;
Galatians 1:8-12; Romans 1:16-17
The Gospel is the Word of God. The Gospel is changeless and sure. The
Gospel is a foundation to build lives upon, and a weapon against Satan. The
Bible is the rule of faith for successful living in the Lord's army. There is no
other Gospel of Christ but that which is found in the Bible. Believing and liv-
ing the Gospel is the strongest fortification in time of trouble. Disobedience
of any part of the Gospel brings trouble to our relationship with God and can
lead to separation from God's army.
MEMORY VERSE: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is
profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righ-
teousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto
all good works.
—2 Timothy 3:16-17
Good News
Jude 3 The Christian life is a warfare. We must fight the good fight of
faith. There are strong and fierce enemies headed by the archenemy—Satan.
How can we be strong to meet them? The first requirement is a perfect and
absolutely dependable Savior. We have this in Jesus Christ. The second re-
quirement is a working program of truth. We must have it as a foundation to
build our lives upon, a weapon to wield against the enemy, and a guide to
show the way through every situation.
Galatians 1:11-12 The Gospel is not rules and regulations that men have
set up, but rules that were given and established through revelation of God
through His Holy Spirit. It is our guide on how to live, how to act, how to
dress, what to do, and all other aspects concerning our Christian activities.
God controls all we do through His Gospel. We cannot change it or rearrange
it. We just take it as it is.
The word gospel is used loosely these days. We hear of the "gospel of
cleanliness" and "gospel of hard work" and many others. Such cannot be gos-
pels. Gospel means "good news." Advice or a command is not news. The
Gospel is something done FOR us, something that comes to us from outside
of ourselves. It is a gift—unearned, undeserved, and unknown before. The
Gospel of Christ is the good news and can be summed up and briefly ex-
pressed in two words, JESUS SAVES. Since there is no other way to be
saved, there is no other Gospel. The Gospel is something to believe, some-
thing to live by, and something to spread to others.
A Sure and Steadfast Hope
Hebrews 6:17-20 God wished to show that His promise was changeless.
First, He gave the promise. Second, He swore by Himself to keep it. In both
of these, it was impossible for God to lie. Nothing could be more sure than
this. Saints are refugees. They have fled from Satan for refuge in God. They
have grasped the hope in God's promise. This hope is an anchor of the soul,
both sure and stedfast. The promise that gives such hope is "the promise of
life which is in Christ Jesus" (2 Timothy 1:1)—spiritual life for the soul now
and life for a new, incorruptible body at Christ's Second Coming (1 Corin-
thians 15:52-54). This life will climax in union with God forever in Heaven.
The promise of all this is the Gospel, the good news.
A Perfect Hope
Hebrews 7:19 Here the law and the Gospel are contrasted. When the
Gospel came—when Jesus came and brought it—it was a better hope be-
cause it made the things of the spirit perfect. It made it possible for men to
draw nigh unto God, to be united in Him. Christ as the Mediator joined men
with God. How? It is by means of once suffering for sins that Christ brings
us to God.
1 Corinthians 15:22 Here is a comparison and contrast. The likeness is
that both death and life came by man—death by the sin of the man, Adam;
life by the sacrifice of the God who became man, Jesus Christ. The contrast
is that death and life are direct opposites. Sin kills the soul. This is tragic.
Christ makes dead souls to live. This is Gospel. He died for all. All can be
saved by accepting Christ's sacrifice.
No Other Gospel
Galatians 1:8 Paul's warning to the Galatian church shows that it is
wrong to listen to, accept, or teach any other gospel than the true one of Je-
sus Christ. Paul was so sure that what he had preached was the true Gospel
that he included himself and the angels in the curse for changing it. How did
he know it was true? Because he received it from "Jesus Christ" (Galatians
1:12). It was revealed to him. This is the basis and guide for all Christian
activities.
A Powerful Gospel
Romans 1:16-17 The gospel of Christ . . . is the power of God unto
salvation. It is the force God uses to bring about salvation. It is the spiritual
law by which the process of salvation works. No one is saved by any other
means. It is God's tool for building His church, which is the army of the
Lord. Since there is but one Gospel, there is but one church. No one can live
a victorious life by any other set of rules or by any book other than the Bible.
It Matters What We Believe
Some say beliefs do not matter just so we are sincere in them. This is to
say that they are not truths but self-built, imaginary philosophies. No, beliefs
mold lives. Only a life built on truth is a good life. And there is only one
truth—that of God. How much power could we expect our U.S. Army to
have if every soldier divided the soldiers' handbook and Articles of War as
people do the Gospel of Christ? It would be as divided, unorganized, and
powerless as the church world is. Disobedience brings serious trouble and
leads to permanent separation from God and Christian fellowship.
JUST A THOUGHT
We are not to add to the Bible,
nor to subtract from it,
but to rightly divide it.
LESSON 3
THE RECRUITING CENTER
Scripture Texts: John 3:3; Colossians 3:1-10; 2 Peter 1:4; 2 Corinthians
The natural person cannot successfully meet the trials and temptations of
life. He has no strength to overcome them. Much less can he meet those
added testings and persecutions that evil times inflict upon the saint who
joins Christ in the battle for truth. No one can be victorious through this bat-
tle unless he has been made new in Christ.
MEMORY VERSE: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to
become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.
—John 1:12
How to Become a New Creature
John 3:3 Except a man be born again—unless he be made new by
God—he cannot be in the Church of God, is not a child of God, and cannot
go to Heaven. Church joining does not put one into the Kingdom of God, nor
does doing good works or enduring suffering or trying hard or being a part
of a spiritual congregation. It is by repentance—by confessing our sins to
God and turning away from them. It is believing on Christ as our Savior, by
trusting Him to cleanse, make alive, and keep us. It is by letting go of our-
selves and surrendering to Him. It is to live thereafter as He leads, to right
wrongs of the past and live holy in the future. No one is drafted into the army
of God. It is a completely voluntary service.
Mortify Your Members
Colossians 3:1-8 If ye then be risen with Christ—this is the resur-
rection of the soul or spirit. This happens when someone hears the Gospel,
repents, believes on Christ, and is saved. He "is passed from death unto life"
(John 5:24). If you are thus risen, seek those things which are above—think
about, love, strive to attain, let grow in your heart the Persons and virtues of
Heaven, where Christ sitteth.
Both God and man have to do with the process of salvation. God works
the inside, death and resurrection. Man regulates his outward members in
accord with it. God, on His part, by grace washes the heart clean of sin and
gives life to the soul. Man, on his part, draws on the power of God to deny
entrance to sinful deeds and to do righteous ones.
When individuals come to the recruiting center, they will not be chosen
until they are ready to die out to earthly things and accept heavenly things.
Saints love heavenly things, not earthly things, because saints are
dead—"dead with Christ from the rudiments of the world" (Colossians 2:20).
Death is separation. Saints are separated, cut off, from worldly things, things
of the flesh, of this life only. Here is death and life. First, in repentance one
dies to sin. He accepts Christ's death for him and is united with Christ in
death to self. He is "baptized into his death" (Romans 6:3), (not baptism in
water but into Christ's death). Second, your life is hid with Christ in God.
The one who dies to sin is made alive in Christ. "If we have been planted to-
gether in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his
resurrection" (Romans 6:5).
Mortify . . . your members which are upon the earth, the earthly, flesh-
ly deeds of natural human nature. Put them to death. Why? Because we have
been made alive in Christ, and we now have power over these works of the
flesh. Some of these works of the flesh are fornication, uncleanness (impure
thoughts, words, and acts that may not be actual fornication but related to
it), inordinate affection (vehement, wrong feelings), evil concupiscence
(strong evil desires, lusts), and covetousness, which is idolatry (loving
possessions rather than God), . . . anger, wrath, malice (desires to bring evil
upon another), blasphemy (dishonor to God), and filthy communication. All
such must be put off, put to death.
A New Soldier
2 Peter 1:4 By accepting God's great and precious promises, we are
made partakers of the divine nature. The old sinful nature is gone, taken
away, and God's nature is given to us. We are saved from sin.
2 Corinthians 5:17 If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature. If we
are not a new creature, we are not in Christ. Through the process called con-
version, a man gives up his life and commits himself to God's leadership and
cause from that time on. Old loves, desires, attitudes, lusts, fears, bondages,
and sins of all kinds are passed away. In their places all things are become
new. Inward virtues, joys, hopes, desires, loves, attitudes, and powers are of
God now.
False Notions
The doctrine that one's position can be in Christ while his deeds are sin-
ful, that Christ's righteousness is imputed unto him even though he is not
righteous, that the divine nature and the sinful nature can live in him at the
same time, the sinful one perhaps predominating, and still the person remain
saved—no, these are false notions. Both the old man (the inner being) and his
deeds (the outward doings) must be put to death. Both the new man inside
and holy actions outside must unite to fill the life. Only then is a person a
child of God and fit for army service for the Lord. Christ's army is made of
changed lives—new men and women.
JUST A THOUGHT
If you think you are too small to do a big thing,
try doing small things in a big way.
LESSON 4
BASIC TRAINING
Scripture Texts: John 4:19-24; Ephesians 3:16-19; James 5:8
God requires service from the heart. True worship must be from the heart
and spirit. We are not children of God unless a work of God is done in our
hearts. The heart must be right and preparation made before we can be sent
out on the battlefield. We must prove true in the small tests before we can be
given greater responsibilities. We need to fix our hearts firmly in Jesus now
to be prepared for persecution and for His coming.
MEMORY VERSE: And, behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you:
but tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be endued with power from on
high.
—Luke 24:49
Inside Experience, Not Outside Form
John 4:19-24 Where should we worship? The woman's interest was
aroused by Jesus' request for a drink, His offer of "living water" (verse 10),
and His knowledge of her past. Perhaps this man could settle a question that
may have bothered her for some time. Was worship in Samaria's mountain
acceptable to God? Would it bring God's favor upon her? Would worship
from Jerusalem bring more favor upon her? Jesus saith . . . the hour com-
eth—God had prescribed in the Law (Exodus 25:8-9; 2 Chronicles 6:6;
7:12-16) that worship should be in Jerusalem, first in the Tabernacle, later
in the Temple. But these buildings were types of the spiritual order that was
to characterize the Gospel dispensation now being brought in. In that hour,
or dispensation, worship would be centered neither in this mountain, nor
yet at Jerusalem. No PLACE would make worship acceptable.
Salvation is of the Jews. It was to the Jews that God had given the earlier
part of His plan, which was to be fulfilled in the coming of Christ to bring
salvation to all men, and make them spiritual Jews—an inside work (Romans
2:28-29). How should we worship? The hour cometh, and now is—right at
that moment and from then on—true worshippers shall worship the Father
in spirit—in their deepest, inmost being and with their feelings, emotions,
motives, and will, rather than in outward places, buildings, ritualistic forms,
and furnishings . . . and in truth—in reality, honestly, without hypocrisy,
felt rather than said only.
Preparation of the Heart
Christianity consists of what God does for man and of what man does for
God in response. Can God need anything from the creature He has made and
given His own breath? The answer is, yes. He desires his companionship. He
hungers for his love. The nature of God requires worship to satisfy it. He
created man for that purpose (Revelation 4:11). In fulfilling that purpose, we
will find our complete salvation and deepest joy. Is there a happier thought
than that we can and may bring pleasure to God? Adam and Eve enjoyed that
rich companionship with God as long as their hearts were responsive to His
will, but sin destroyed that sweet fellowship.
Because God used the Tabernacle and Temple and outward forms of ser-
vice, we may think that in the Law dispensation He desired outward worship.
No, then, as now, He looked deep into hearts to find the gift that would satis-
fy Him. He commanded Israel to "fear" and "love" and "serve" Him "with all
thy heart and with all thy soul" (Deuteronomy 10:12). His eyes "run to and
fro," seeking those "whose heart is perfect toward him" (2 Chronicles 16:9).
He said, "I . . . search the heart, I try the reins" (Jeremiah 17:10). He "de-
sirest truth in the inward parts" (Psalm 51:6).
The Basics
Ephesians 3:16-19 Paul, writing from prison, told us as beloved brethren
how to be strong in the Lord and go forward to victory in the battle ahead.
Be strengthened . . . by his Spirit in the inner man; that Christ may dwell
in your hearts . . . rooted and grounded in love . . . be filled with all the
fulness of God. None of these are an outward gift of material things. They
are inside things of the heart.
James 5:8 Be ye . . . patient (bearing or enduring without complaint,
expectant without discontent, not hasty, persevering, diligent, unwearied).
Consider how patience fits us to fight the Christian warfare. Jesus, in warn-
ing of betrayal, persecution, and tribulation, said, "In your patience possess
ye your souls" (Luke 21:19). "Patience" performs a "perfect work" (James
1:4). Stablish your hearts—before a hurricane, people fasten down their
property, making it firm and sure, so as to withstand the coming storm.
We need life and holiness and strength to meet the challenges of daily life
and the threat of the storm that is upon us. Life and strength must have a
source. Indications point to the approach of an intense struggle with Satan.
To endure a time of trial, temptation, and tribulation, we need the Gospel and
a genuine experience of salvation. This will draw increased persecutions to
us. Satan hates the Gospel. But believing, accepting, and obeying it brings
the living power of Christ into your life. A Christian's diet has much to do
with his power to stand in time of battle (Hebrews 6:5). By receiving the
living power of Christ, we are set free spiritually (John 8:36). He has that
anchor of hope joining him with Heaven and holding him steady (Hebrews
Friend, repent and open your heart to the Savior. Take Him. Be prepared
for whatever may come.
JUST A THOUGHT
"If one cannot find peace within,
it is useless to seek for it elsewhere." —M.F. Boyd
LESSON 5
A GOOD SOLDIER
Scripture Texts: 1 Corinthians 2:1-5; 15:10; 2 Corinthians 4:1-9; 2 Timo-
The world needs a church that has contact with God, living truth, and
power. Much is called the church that is not the church. If we have not a su-
pernatural church, we have no church at all. If God is not moving in a peo-
ple, they are not the Church of God. His power in the church is evidenced by
changed lives and answered prayers. Life is there. The early church was a
powerful church moved by God. When God shakes off the imitations and the
dust clears away, the true church will still be standing firm in Him.
MEMORY VERSE: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is
come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and
in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
—Acts 1:8
Christ, the Power and Wisdom of God
1 Corinthians 2:1-5 Paul had come to Corinth declaring the Gospel of
Christ. Now, writing later, he said he came not with excellency of
speech . . . wisdom . . . or enticing words. Although Paul was an educated
man, he did not display his learning in his preaching. Instead, he came in
weakness . . . fear, and . . . trembling. Why? Knowledge of Jesus Christ,
and him crucified is greater than any knowledge. The demonstration of the
Spirit and of power is greater than anything man's wisdom can do. Paul
cast aside his own wisdom that God might work mightily through him. The
faith of the people must not be based upon the wisdom of men—Paul's
reasoning powers, the drawing power of his personality, his knowledge. Their
faith must be in the power of God—in what they saw God doing in Paul and
others and especially in the work they felt Him doing in their own hearts.
Faith in anything else could be shaken by opposite reasoning, a stronger
personality, superior knowledge, or the discouragements of Satan.
We need power greater than human power to live and work for God and
to be good soldiers to meet Satan's opposition. We receive the needed power
from the baptism of the Holy Spirit. All we do must be done by God through
us, not by us.
Power by the Grace of God
1 Corinthians 15:10 Each of us has (1) a life to live, (2) a work to do,
and (3) opposition to meet. The LIFE is to be yielded to Christ for redemp-
tion and lived to glorify God. The WORK is to take the Gospel of Christ to
all people. The OPPOSITION is Satan's constant attempt to destroy our
LIFE and prevent our WORK from being effective. He will use all means,
from common temptation and trial to the fiercest persecution. That we may
carry out these three charges, God has provided an Almighty Savior, a true
Gospel, a perfect salvation, and the power to do what these require.
Three times in this Scripture, Paul spoke of the grace of God. First, that
grace—the free bestowal of God's life and gifts upon him—made him the
man he was, gave him purity of heart and talents, and called him to be an
Apostle. Second, God's grace was the source and power producing all the ac-
complishments of Paul's life—the souls saved, churches established, miracles
wrought, and healings done (Matthew 9:6-8). Thirdly, lest some credit these
to Paul's own working, he emphasized—yet not I, but the grace of God.
This is witnessed by what Paul was, not in his own strength but through God.
2 Corinthians 4:1-9 We have this treasure—this ministry . . . handling
the word of God, the commission to preach the Gospel—in earthen ves-
sels—in human bodies and minds, compared to containers of clay, easily
broken. We have power to tell men the truth even when personal harm may
be at stake, when men oppose it (Micah 3:8; Romans 1:16). God uses such
so that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us. Being
human, the servant may be troubled . . . perplexed. . . persecuted . . . cast
down. But because God is given freedom to work, the servant is not dis-
tressed . . . not in despair . . . not forsaken . . . not destroyed.
Peter and the other disciples presented a sorry picture of fear and defeat
at Christ's Crucifixion. Afterward they bravely met threats, beatings, prison,
and death. What made the difference? They had been baptized with the Holy
Spirit. "Perfect love casteth out fear" (1 John 4:18). We can have the same
power by having Him Who is power. There is no other way. We cannot im-
itate Him. We must have Him within by being saved from sin by the blood
of Jesus Christ, and by yielding all to God to use as He will and opening our
heart for His Spirit's entrance.
The Power to Endure
In our memory verse today, Jesus, just before leaving the world, repeated
His promise of power to His disciples. This power was so necessary to their
future life and work that they must not leave Jerusalem until they had re-
ceived it. This is the power we have been reading about today. All the Apos-
tles were given it before starting their work. We must also.
2 Timothy 2:3-4 A good soldier of Jesus must endure hard things. He
must be in good spiritual shape. As a natural soldier must have disruption of
his family life, his daily routine, and lifestyle, so must we as good soldiers
of Christ. A good soldier of God does not become so entangled with the af-
fairs of this life that he cannot get loose to please Him Who has chosen him
to be a soldier. Saints must be careful not to become entangled with legit-
imate things that are necessary in our everyday living.
1 Peter 4:10-11 As every man hath received the gift—the gift of the
Spirit, the spiritual ability to do our part of God's work—minister the same
one to another—do that work and so bless others. We are only stewards of
the grace of God. We only hold these powers and gifts in trust. Whatever we
do we must do as of the ability which God giveth, not our own. We must
abase ourselves and exalt God—that God in all things may be glorified
through Jesus Christ. Nothing less than the power of the Holy Spirit is
sufficient for these things. This was Peter's experience. It can be yours.
JUST A THOUGHT
There can be but one truth.
LESSON 6
THE UNIFORM
Scripture Text: Ephesians 6:10-18
The Christian is in a real war against Satan. Our enemies are spiritual.
Our weapons must be spiritual. We must have the power of God, not our
own. Faith and power are necessary to the working of each of our pieces of
armor.
As each member of the Church of God seriously considers the issues of
this life in Christ, he must realize that the purest strength and fortitude are
necessary to worthily and successfully fight the battle that faces us. In the
Book of Ephesians, God caused Paul to prepare an excellent outline of that
strength and the secrets to finding it.
MEMORY VERSE: Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to
stand against the wiles of the devil.
—Ephesians 6:11
The Whole Armor of God
Ephesians 6:10-13 The most essential secret of receiving strength is to
know that it MUST come from the Lord. Why do we need fighting strength?
Because we have enemies, chief over them is the devil. Under him are prin-
cipalities and powers influencing government, society, and trends of
thought; rulers of the darkness of this world—the devil controlling the
agencies of sin and evil; spiritual wickedness in high places—leaders who
have no respect for God and His Word, who corrupt the Gospel. Men and
women are the tools, but Satan is behind it all. Our soul's enemies are not
flesh and blood—not physical to be fought with literal weapons—but
spiritual. We must have spiritual weapons, the whole armour of God. These
equip us to withstand Satan's agents in the evil day—time of severe attack.
And having done all that is possible for us to do, or having overcome all, to
stand—to hold firm, to keep our faith in God. Sometimes we must stand still
that we may see the power of God and hold our spiritual position.
We are in enemy country. Satan is the god of this world and the whole
world is in wickedness. Paul exhorted us to fight the good fight of faith.
Faith is a spiritual weapon which the enemy cannot handle.
Where does the strength of a Christian lie? If it is not a borrowed
strength, it is no strength at all. Only as we yield up our own little power and
look to God to supply us, can we have any effect against the enemy. Trying
in our own strength only hinders God. His strength is made perfect in our
weakness as we give up our strength to take His (2 Corinthians 12:9). Can
we in any other way come through temptation, tribulation, persecution, and
death victoriously?
The Armor of Defense
The five defensive pieces of armor are named first. A soldier is identified
by the uniform he wears and the weapons he uses. This is so with the Chris-
tian. The Christian's equipment is the best and the most up to date. Paul
looked at the armor worn by the soldier guarding him and was reminded of
the Christian soldier's armor, which he outlined in our lesson today.
Ephesians 6:14 To stand we must be girt about with truth, encircled
with it, holding the rest of the armor in place. God is true, His Word is truth,
His truth sets free, and truth is strong and eternal. The breastplate is righ-
teousness—the quality of being right, without sin. Righteousness, not one's
own but the holiness imparted by God, protects the spiritual heart from death
through sin.
Ephesians 6:15 Feet are for going. Soldiers wore brazen boots to protect
the feet and legs and enable them to travel in hard places. The spiritual feet
of a saint are his going forth with the gospel of peace to give it to others at
home and afar (Isaiah 52:7). The peace is inner peace, the peace of God in
the heart that God gives even in the midst of outer turmoil. The Gospel is
both the saint's protection and his message. It is not just the bare facts of
Christ's death and resurrection to save us. It is the preparation of this, the
Gospel accepted into one's heart, lived, grown, beautified, made visible, and
living. Doctrine alone is not nearly so powerful in winning souls as doctrine
demonstrated and adorned by the beauty of a holy life (Titus 2:10).
Ephesians 6:16 Above all—most important—taking the shield of faith.
The shield was held in front of one, protecting the whole body. Faith is
spiritual protection against Satan. Why is faith above all? Because it is the
belief that grasps the supply of the grace of God. By it all other pieces are
made effective. Without faith, no grace can be active in our lives. With it we
turn aside all the fiery darts of the wicked one.
Ephesians 6:17a The helmet protects the head. The head is the director
of the body, the seat of understanding. Salvation, the spiritual helmet, gives
purpose and worth and a goal to the direction of the life. It opens the under-
standing to truth. It protects from wandering in error.
The Weapons of Offense
Ephesians 6:17b One offensive weapon named is the sword of the
Spirit. A sword is to kill and destroy the enemy. The sword referred to here
is the spiritual sword, the word of God, the Bible. It is most dangerous,
spiritually, for us to attempt to use the Spirit's sword without proper super-
vision by the Spirit. The Holy Spirit inspired it (2 Timothy 3:16-17; 2 Peter
1:21). The Holy Spirit enables us to teach it (1 Peter 4:10-11). The Holy
Spirit brings the hearer to understand and obey it (1 Corinthians 2:10-11).
The Bible is a weapon to kill sin and destroy the work of Satan (Hebrews
Ephesians 6:18 Praying always. Another offensive weapon is continual
communion with God. Prayer is the motivating power that keeps all the de-
fensive armor active and effective. It is the means by which faith reaches to
God to bring His help. Faith prompts prayer, and prayer increases faith,
producing constant nourishment, life, and growth. Prayer MUST be in the
Spirit. We should pray for saints to hold true and sinners to be saved.
Can we use the Bible if we do not know the Bible? How can we and our
children come to know it? Can we leave them to face greater blasphemies and
fiercer persecutions than we ever faced without knowledge of how to with-
stand them? The little teaching of Sunday school is not enough. Where does
God lay the burden of learning and teaching His Word? (Ephesians 6:4; Deu-
teronomy 6:6-7).
Satan is waging savage, worldwide war against God and His church.
When his evil artillery is suddenly turned on us, will we meet him in God's
armor and wielding God's sword? Will our faith and prayers make our fight
effective?
JUST A THOUGHT
The average man can do more harm
with his mouth than with a gun.
LESSON 7
READY FOR SERVICE
Scripture Texts: Matthew 10:1-8; Mark 16:15-20; Psalm 126:5-6; 1 Peter
When Jesus told the Apostles they would be His witnesses, He told them
to spread the good news of salvation. This same commission is directed to
every soldier of Christ today. The work of Jesus is the teaching of the king-
dom throughout the world. No one has the power to go forth and witness
until he has received power of the Holy Ghost (Acts 1:8). God has entrusted
part of His own life and qualities to His people. He comes in to work and live
in human hearts. We must account to Him for our handling of this gift.
MEMORY VERSE: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all
the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.
—Matthew 24:14
Christ Gives Power to Witness
Matthew 10:1-8 Christ called His disciples. He chose twelve for special
work. We are called out under the same conditions. All God's work is spe-
cial. He ordained them, that they should be with Him, and that He might send
them forth to witness for Him. He gave them power against unclean spirits.
These spirits are demons and have greater power than humans. No human
can withstand them without the power of God. And He gave them power to
heal—neither can a human do this in his own power. All were common work-
ing men, "unlearned and ignorant" (Acts 4:13).
Go not into the way of the Gentiles . . . Samaritans. This was a tempor-
ary command for this trip. Paul afterward was to go to the Gentiles, adding

Preach . . . The kingdom of heaven is at hand—it was even then being

armies, or material things. It is "righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Ho-
ly Ghost" (Romans 14:17). What a message we have to deliver to the world!
Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils—not only
are these spiritual works, but also they can be seen with the natural eye.
Christ Commanded "Go"
Mark 16:15-20 Near the time of His Ascension Jesus gave instruction to
His disciples, and it is our instruction also. Go ye into all the world, and
preach the gospel to every creature. No one is to be left out. They were to
start, and we are to follow and carry on until all is finished. This charge is
laid upon all the church. It takes brave people to be trusted soldiers for
Christ. Just anyone will not do. Witnessing begins at home, then to the neigh-
bors, and finally to the whole world. We may, as Jesus did, receive the least
honor from our own people.
Before we will be entrusted with the large, or the most important work,
we must learn to be faithful in the smaller things God will ask us to do. Jesus
always works with His people, never sends them alone. With this command,
He promised some signs that would follow them that believe. Beware of work
being done where the signs go before, exalting man (healing campaigns). He
promised power to cast out devils, speak with new tongues (languages), heal
the sick, and immunity to snakebite and other poisons (accidentally received).
These were to be had by faith in Jesus' name.
Reward for Our Labor
Psalm 126:5-6 They that sow in tears—in sacrifice, hardship, opposi-
tion, or persecution—shall reap in joy, the joy of winning souls to the Mas-
ter. To do this, we must carry precious seed, the truth of the Gospel. No
"social gospel," or human creed, or theory of developing the good in man, or
mere suffering will do. It must be the living message of salvation through Je-
sus' blood by faith and repentance.
In the memory verse for today Jesus states, "And this gospel of the king-
dom shall be preached in all the world . . . unto all nations." This is in accord
with the prophecy in Nebuchadnezzar's dream. "The stone . . . became a
great mountain, and filled the whole earth" (Daniel 2:34-35, 44). The King-
dom of God will be victorious and will stand forever. What part will we have
in this victory?
To God Be the Glory
1 Peter 4:10-11 As we have received, so we are to minister. Whatever
gift, ability, or opportunity God gives us is to be used. Our purpose in using
is to serve others of the church or of the world. The end goal is to bring prof-
it to the Lord. The gifts are grace. They are of the life of God—portions of
His power, ability, and nature put into us. They are made up of many
forms—teaching, preaching, faith, healing, wisdom, discernment, governing
ability, and many others. They are not limited to the nine Paul mentioned in
1 Corinthians, Chapter 12. Any tool God supplies and enables us to use for
service is part of His manifold grace. We are caretakers of them. We must
be good stewards.
We must exercise our gift with the ability that God gives. Look to Him,
not ourselves, for ability. Lean on Him; ask for His leading and help. Jesus
said, "Without me ye can do nothing" (John 15:5). The end purpose is that
God may be glorified. When we are used in service and others are benefitted,
when God gets the glory, then the grace is working as planned. "But the man-
ifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal" (1 Corinthians

What message do you carry? By what authority?
LESSON 8
FACING THE ENEMY
Scripture Texts: Mark 3:1-6; Acts 13:6-12; Matthew 10:16-36
The work of the church is to seek and to save the lost. Christ instructs
those He sends and tells them that all will meet persecution. He tells us this
so that we will know what to expect.
First of all, we must know who our enemy really is. Spiritual discernment
is very needful. The devil may attack as a roaring lion or come as a wolf in
sheep's clothing. He is spoken of as an angel of light. We can recognize the
moves of Satan only with the understanding of the Word of God and the
guiding of the Holy Spirit.
MEMORY VERSE: Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came
not to send peace, but a sword.
—Matthew 10:34
Jesus Is Our Example
Mark 3:1-6 Jesus, our example, went into the synagogue in Capernaum
and was about to heal the man with a withered hand. Immediately the battle
lines were set between good and evil. The faultfinders, the Pharisees, were
already decided against Jesus. They wanted Him to heal the man so they
could accuse Him of breaking the Sabbath.
Beaten at their own scheme, the Pharisees sought the Herodians and with
them plotted ways to kill Jesus. Satan's forces, which cannot get along among
themselves, will come together in false unity to fight against the truth. How
easily we all—even saints—can fall into the sin of an accusing spirit. Let us
watch our hearts, examining as to whether discovery of a fault in another
gives us pain or pleasure. Watch and pray.
Jesus showed courage. He did not turn from His plan because of op-
position. He did not fight His enemies with carnal weapons. We can learn
from Him in our own meeting of opposition from the enemy's forces.
Holy Boldness
Acts 13:6-12 Paul looked the enemy right straight in the face and named
Elymas out as a false prophet, a child of the devil, and an enemy of all righ-
teousness. Satan yet today transforms his false prophets into angels of
so-called light (2 Corinthians 11:14-15). This severe rebuke was from the
Holy Spirit speaking through Paul. As Elymas was smote with blindness for
propagating a perverted doctrine, so people yet today grope in darkness and
blindness when they resist the truth. The deputy was astonished at the clear
doctrine of the Lord, and he believed. The straight, clear Gospel of Christ
will still cast Satan out and cause honest hearts to believe and be won over
to God.
When the serpent's head is bruised, be assured he will strike back; he will
bruise our heel. When those in high places see a prosperous work being done,
they will become envious. They will contradict and blaspheme the message.
To agree or to disagree is each individual's privilege, but the good seed has
been sown.
The Threefold Secret of Victory
Matthew 10:16-28 Jesus did not tell His followers of any generation that
the Christian way would be easy. The fact that Christians are in warfare lets
one know that life will be filled with conflict. Paul told Timothy to "endure
hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ" (2 Timothy 2:3).
Being sent out among wolves is not an easy way for sheep to go. The only
thing they have to protect them is a good shepherd. Let us look into the
threefold secret of victory: (1) Wisdom and guilelessness . . . wise as
serpents, and harmless as doves. "The serpent was more subtil than any
beast of the field" (Genesis 3:1), hence, the serpent's association with wis-
dom. Christians were also to be harmless. The Greek version says "guileless-
ness," a character in which there is no alloy. (2) Absolute confidence in the
Director . . . take no thought. These words indicate Jesus' tender sympathy
with the feelings of the unlearned disciples, while standing before those who
were counted so superior to them in power and knowledge. Christ promised
He would tell them what they should say and also how they should say it. (3)
Steadfast and final perseverance. We must endure as long as the trial lasts;
if necessary, to the end of our lives. God is greater than our enemies. One
joined to Him need not fear them. As we share with Christ in suffering, we
will share with Him in victory.
Fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell—a refer-
ence to the Divine. This verse is speaking of the One who makes the final
disposition of the soul AND body. This only occurs on the Resurrection Day
when "there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust"
(Acts 24:15). On that Day, the bodies of the departed will come forth and be
reunited with "ten thousands ['myriads'; The Emphatic Greek Diaglott] of his
saints" (Jude 14). Myriads are defined as "any indefinitely large number"
(Webster's New World Dictionary). He will return with the souls to be re-
united with the bodies.
The Greek word hell used here is Gehenna. This word is only used in an
after Judgment Day setting. Matthew 5:29-30 is a vivid example of this:
"whole body should be cast into hell [Gehenna]." This only occurs after "we
. . . all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive
the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be
good or bad" (2 Corinthians 5:10).
This portion of the verse reveals the reverential fear we should have for
the Divine (God, Christ, and His Word). If we accord Them the proper place
in our lives, we will never need to fear anyone or anything! Jesus clearly said
in Luke 10:19, "Behold, I give you power . . . over all the power of the
