Our Greatest Enemies
One of the greatest battlefields we will face is in our own minds. Here we
have the great battle with self, our greatest enemy. Self is constantly coming
on the scene, exalting itself against the knowledge of God. We must bring
every thought into captivity to be able to obey Christ (2 Corinthians 10:5).
Matthew 10:36 Our own loved ones may betray us to the enemies of
Christ, through fear or false teaching. This is happening many times. Choose
Christ first. We must neither abandon Christ to please them or deny Christ
for fear of them. If we do not love Christ above all, we are not worthy of
Him and will be cast out. Matthew 10:39 brings a very pointed message: He
that lives shall die and he that dies shall live. Every person is either dead to
Christ and joined to self or dead to self and joined to Christ.
Souls cannot be won over to God without battling the forces that oppose
Christ. We must "earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered
unto the saints" (Jude 3).
JUST A THOUGHT
The only way to settle a disagreement is
on the basis of what is right—not who is right.
LESSON 9
GOOD SOLDIERS DON'T QUIT
Scripture Texts: 1 Corinthians 16:13; 2 Timothy 2:1-5; Hebrews 12:4;
1 Peter 1:13; Luke 18:8
We must be strong, manly, and faithful before great opposition and dan-
ger. How can we do this? Trying hard and determination are not enough.
Paul, speaking of hard places in life, said, "I can do all things through Christ
which strengtheneth me" (Philippians 4:13). God gave much of the answer
to this question when He spoke through Isaiah in Isaiah 40:31.
Today we look further into God's instructions for fighting the Christian
warfare and for preparing to meet the most violent attacks of Satan.
MEMORY VERSE: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be
strong.
—1 Corinthians 16:13
Be Strong
1 Corinthians 16:13 Watch ye. Watch self to stay holy and the heart to
stay true. Watch God to obey Him, others that we do our duty to them, and
the enemies of our souls that they do not lead us from the old paths. Stand
fast in the faith—"in one spirit," unity and love (Philippians 1:27); "in the
Lord," living in Him (Philippians 4:1); in the faith, or belief in the gospel
(1 Corinthians 15:1-4) and in all the Word of God. Quit you like men. It
takes brave, strong, courageous, unflinching, faithful men and women to
fight victoriously in this Christian warfare. The quitters are weak, fearful,
doubting, tossed to and fro like children by every wind of doctrine, and never
settled on the foundation that is sure. Be strong—strong not in ourselves but
in the Lord. Do not yield to sin in any form.
The Strength Is in Jesus Christ
2 Timothy 2:1-3 Paul wrote to his young fellow laborer Timothy, Be
strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus—in the life of God imparted to
him. No one can be spiritually strong except by the gift of life from Christ.
The things that thou hast heard . . . commit thou to faithful men. Pass on
the Gospel to others that they may be faithful to it. It must be spread to all
people. Endure hardness. Satan is determined to defeat us. It takes active
resistance to withstand him. It takes the power of God. We must be firm, de-
termined to take any difficulty or suffering, and not yield. Jesus gives us a
great promise in Matthew 24:13.
Warfare Calls for a Separation
2 Timothy 2:4-5 No man that warreth entangleth himself. No good
soldier becomes entangled with his own interests. Every personal interest,
business, or activity must be dropped to free him for fighting. Dear ones,
cannot we see how necessary it is that we drop every selfish interest and
worldly ambition and pursuit if we are to please him who hath chosen us?
He said, "Whosoever . . . forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my dis-
ciple" (Luke 14:33).
We are to be separated from and to—from self and the world to Christ,
that we may please Him. To do so we must strive lawfully—according to
His rules. Only by obeying the Bible and the voice of the Holy Spirit can we
gain "the crown of life" (James 1:12). When God asks us to forsake all that
we have, to resist evil unto blood and with our lives, and to endure faithful
unto the end, He is not asking too much. Compare what others ask and what
they give in return. Communism demands that one surrender property, free-
dom, chosen pursuits, home, children, truth, hope, faith, God, and the Savior
with no reward. Tyrants press their claims by force and cruelty. God uses
love and gives all things in return—"joy unspeakable and full of glory"
(1 Peter 1:8), in "the life that now is, and of that which is to come" (1 Timo-
What Is Asked of Us?
Hebrews 12:4 Hebrews, Chapter 11, lists many faithful saints of God
who labored, suffered, and died for their faith, "not accepting deliverance"
(verse 35) by compromise. We sometimes speak of them as the "Who's Who
of Faith." They and Jesus Himself are held up as examples to inspire and
encourage us to follow. There is no limit set for the suffering we must endure
before dropping our resistance to sin. Jesus stopped at nothing, but gave His
life. Though we may have suffered, most of us have not yet resisted unto
blood—not suffered physical injury or death. God will go with us making the
way before us, but we must resist sin with our all (1 Corinthians 10:13).
1 Peter 1:13 Wherefore—because of the greatness of the salvation we
are discussing—gird up the loins of your mind. We might compare this
girding up to rolling up our sleeves to begin work. The Christian girds up his
mind by drawing in all wandering, idle, foolish thoughts and concentrating
upon the main purpose of serving Christ and conquering Satan, determined
to win. Be sober—alert and serious in taking responsibility. Think seriously,
take heed, and give careful attention to God's commands. Soberness is not
gloom. It is depth and seriousness. Hope to the end—constantly keep in
view with hope—the grace—the gift of God—to be brought . . . at the rev-
elation of Jesus Christ—when Jesus is seen at His Second Coming. What
gift will He bring His redeemed ones then? For this glorious hope, we are to
gird our minds.
Anchoring Our Position
There is a spirit prevalent today that fears sober thought. Talk about God,
prayer, or anything, it says, but do not get serious. Shy away from
old-fashioned duty, responsibility, sorrow for sin, or dependence on God.
Have fun today, do not think of tomorrow, avoid intense feeling or deep
concern. Do not go to extremes or be fanatic. This is not right.
Luke 18:8 As the coming of Christ draws near, Satan is intensifying his
efforts to destroy faith in God. He has many methods. Unbelief and
blasphemy grow more extreme. Many presuming to speak for God's church
voice denials of Christ and the Bible under pretense of improved inter-
pretation. How can we anchor our position and that of our children, so as not
to be shaken loose by Satan's cruel forces? We must know what we believe
and where we stand. Life is real, and life is earnest. We cannot live it in
lightness and escape the judgments of God (Hebrews 2:1-3).
A. B. Simpson tells of a painting showing a beautiful French girl and her
Protestant lover on the night before the terrible massacre of St. Bartholo-
mew. With tears she tries to pin a Catholic badge on his breast as protection
from the swords of the assassins. He gently holds back her hand and unpins
the badge, knowing they probably will never meet again on earth. He was
quitting himself like a man. And God saw.
JUST A THOUGHT
Faith is no lone traveler, she will not go
except hand in hand with Obedience.
LESSON 10
NEVER LOOK BACK
Scripture Texts: Luke 9:62, Hebrews 12:25-29; 1 Corinthians 10:13;
Philippians 3:13-14; Mark 13:13
He who turns from following Christ loses his salvation. God is going to
allow severe testings to shake off the weak and false, and keep the strong and
true. God has provided means, through His grace, whereby we may stand.
We must endure to the end to be finally saved.
Prayer is often requested for the unsaved. This is good, but we must also
pray for the saints. (Read Ephesians 6:18; 2 Timothy 1:3.) Think back to
many seemingly strong saints who made a strong start, but failed to finish the
race. This is why we should pray for one another. As Satan's attacks in-
crease, how much will our prayers for ourselves and for each other affect our
enduring unto the end?
MEMORY VERSE: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but
this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching
forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the
prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
—Philippians 3:13-14
Hand to the Plow
Luke 9:62 When a man starts to plow a field, he plans a straight line and
sets a point on the farther side toward which to drive. To take his eyes from
that point and look back would turn him from the straight course. He would
miss the goal. Jesus, in the previous five verses, had been talking with three
who wanted to follow Him if it did not require a complete break with their
former lives. Jesus made it clear that no one can serve Him without a clean
break with sin and complete dedication to Him. God has laid a straight line
for us to plow spiritually—a holy life for us to live. He set a goal for us to
work toward—eternal life with Him. One who starts the Christian life, then
looks back, wishing again for the world's pleasures and comforts, is not a fit
member of God's kingdom—he is not a child of God. The words are looking
back, present tense. While he is looking, he is unfit. He can repent of his
looking back (backsliding), if he has not gone too far, and again plow a
straight furrow. But many, yes most, never do. It is dangerous to look back.
"REMEMBER LOT'S WIFE" (Luke 17:32). (Read Genesis 19:1-26.)
A Final Shaking Off
Hebrews 12:25-29 Those who refused, or disobeyed, him that spake on
earth—Moses, the mediator of the old covenant—were punished. Much
greater punishment will be for those who turn away from him that speaketh
from heaven—Jesus, the Mediator of the new covenant, the Gospel (John
1:17). Jesus spoke from Heaven because He came from Heaven (John 8:23).
God's voice . . . shook the earth when He gave the Law on Mount Sinai.
Now He promises to shake once more both earth and heaven. (Read Haggai
2:6-7.) Why? To remove all that can be shaken off and keep all that are so
firmly anchored they cannot be shaken loose. Things that are made—made
by man, purely human, of the earth, will be shaken off. The things of God
will remain, people who are born of God and led by His Spirit.
How can we be ones who remain? God's kingdom cannot be moved. In
it, He reigns in the hearts of His saved ones. He provides grace sufficient to
withstand all shakings. Let us have grace—take it, use it. Without it we
cannot serve God acceptably. "God receives no burnt offering not kindled
by fire from His own altar" (Adam Clarke).
Since there is such great danger in looking or turning back, we cannot
afford to let conditions and situations affect our position with God. God's
grace is sufficient for us (2 Corinthians 12:9). We cannot afford to allow our
position to depend upon our companions. Their strength is not sufficient for
us. Their weakness can pull us down. We need one another's prayers, but
God has so designed that we can make it if no one else prays for us. If we
use the grace He gives us now, He will give more as needed. We stand by be-
ing filled with the Holy Spirit—"this grace wherein we stand" (Romans 5:2).
A Way to Escape
1 Corinthians 10:13 Satan pursues us to tempt and destroy. Looking
back is a spiritual condition that begins in the mind. Actions depend on
thoughts. Thoughts of evil will weaken one's hold on God, and he will fall
when the shaking time comes. God is faithful . . . with the temptation, He
makes a way to escape. He supplies grace equal to the need. To avoid sin
and do what is right, look for the way to escape. It is always there. No one
can say when he falls into sin, "I can't help it." When God sees faith and a
desire for a way out, He opens the way—always.
Reward for Enduring
Philippians 3:13-14 Paul had not yet finished his course, completed his
work, or obtained his crown. So he pressed on toward the mark or goal to
which God called him. With strong exertion, he cut out all other interests. He
did not even look to the left or to the right. Forgetting . . . things . . . be-
hind—Paul did not neglect obligations or fail to make things right. He did
not look back to the world in indecision, nor turn in desire to his old life of
companions. When he repented, he left the old life and began a new one. As
Paul kept his eyes on the mark, so must we. That mark is Jesus.
Mark 13:13 Ye shall be hated—the Church of God and the people of the
world are on opposite sides. Different spirits motivate them; they serve dif-
ferent masters. Therefore the world hates the church as it hates Christ. For
my name's sake—because we are His. He that shall endure—continue unto
the end in the life of faith—he shall be saved. He shall receive the final
phase of salvation: the resurrection of the body in an incorruptible state, en-
trance to Heaven, and a crown of life. No promise of this is ever given to
anyone who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back and goes into sin.
It is for those only whom death finds abiding in Christ.
Are we praying for those who persecute our brethren and ourselves as we
are praying for our brethren who are being persecuted? Is not the reward
worth the commitment?
JUST A THOUGHT
No farmer ever plowed a field
by turning it over in his mind.
LESSON 11
STRANGERS AND PILGRIMS ON THE EARTH
Scripture Texts: Hebrews 11:8-16; 1 Peter 2:9-11; 1 John 2:15-17
Our conversation is in Heaven. God's people are hid with Christ in God.
Their lives are anchored in Heaven. Their citizenship is there (Philippians
3:20). This is what all Christians have in common that makes their fellow-
ship possible. Saints of God are oddballs, misfits, square pegs in round
holes, so to speak. This is because the world does not know them. Jesus calls
saints salt, light, and a city set on a hill. God's people are citizens of Heaven
and dependent upon God.
MEMORY VERSE: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed
upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world
knoweth us not, because it knew him not.
—1 John 3:1
Abraham's Faith and Hope
Hebrews 11:8-16 By faith Abraham . . . obeyed the calling of God to
go out, not knowing where. Abraham had no knowledge of what was ahead.
All he had was God's command and promise (Genesis 12:1-3). It was either
to obey God in faith or to disobey. He trusted God. He sojourned—dwelt
temporarily—in Canaan—as in a strange country. It was not home to Abra-
ham. He lived in tabernacles—temporary dwellings—to the end of his life.
Why? Because he believed that God's promise reached farther than the land
of Canaan. He looked for a city . . . whose builder and maker is God—the
Kingdom of God both on earth and in Heaven. His spiritual vision let him see
that Canaan, while it was literally given to Abraham's family, was also a
type of a greater, spiritual possession. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob held their
faith through their journey here. By faith they saw, were persuaded of, and
embraced the promises. By claiming to be strangers and pilgrims here, they
showed their desire for the heavenly country. They never got to see or inherit
that country, but we have found it, and are a part of it, thank God. That city
which hath foundations is based on sure, true, good, and eternal footing
(Ephesians 2:19-20).
The Church of God is the city that Abraham saw by faith. Its builder is
God. Jesus said, "I will build my church" (Matthew 16:18). It is a heavenly
country that is existing on earth for a time (Ephesians 3:15).
The Church on Earth
Among the questions that enter our thoughts is why opposition, trials, and
persecution are the lot of the Church of God. To answer this question, we
must remember that this is a corrupted world. It is no longer good as God
created it. This places the church in the middle of "the whole world [that]
lieth in wickedness" (1 John 5:19).
1 Peter 2:9-11 The Church of God on the earth is traveling to Heaven.
God's people are a chosen generation. His people are of one generation and
are holy (Ephesians 1:4). They are a royal priesthood. Jesus Christ "hath
made us kings and priests unto God" (Revelation 1:6). As kings, saints reign
over sin. As priests, they draw near to God and intercede in behalf of those
in sin. The offering that the saints, or priests, bring to God is the "living
sacrifice" of themselves (Romans 12:1) and "the sacrifice of praise" (He-
brews 13:15). An holy nation—separated unto God, cleansed from sin, righ-
teous. A peculiar people—God's own private property, belonging to Him
alone, responsible to Him only.
These terms describe the Church of God in the Gospel dispensation. Com-
pare with the description of Israel, God's special people in the Law dispensa-
tion (Exodus 19:5-6; Deuteronomy 7:6).
The purpose of people being transformed into this kind of people is to
show forth the praises of God by word and by life. In time past, they were
not a people—the Gentile nations were not accepted under the law but now
the Gospel is for all people. The people of God are different and separate
from the people of the world. They have come out of darkness into his
marvelous light. We must abstain from fleshly lusts. We cannot be at home
in both the world and in Heaven. The interest and attention of a true saint of
God are set upon Heavenly objects, not upon selfish pleasures or worldly
possessions. He uses earthly things only as temporary tools to serve Jesus on
his journey through this country to Heaven.
The Saints' Program
1 John 2:15-17 Love not the world because it and its lust pass away and
leave us empty, without value or hope. He that doeth the will of God abid-
eth for ever—has eternal life. He builds on eternal things. No one can love
the world and love the Father also. There are two ways open: to love the
world or to do the will of God. Which will we choose? Build for eternity, not
for this world.
We cannot have a vision of the kingdom simply by desiring it. We cannot
be a stranger and pilgrim on the earth just by calling himself one. We are not
a foreigner to the world unless we are citizens "of the household of God"
(Ephesians 2:19). We become a citizen of Heaven by taking Christ who is the
way to the Father (John 14:6). Only the Spirit of God can take love of the
world out of our hearts and fill us with love for God and Heaven. Abraham
was a stranger and pilgrim on the earth. He saw by faith the establishment
of God's kingdom on earth and in Heaven. Why can't we?
JUST A THOUGHT
It is better to look ahead and prepare
than to look back and regret.
LESSON 12
FINAL VICTORY GAINED
Scripture Texts: Hebrews 3:12-14; 10:26-38; 2 Timothy 4:6-8
The saddest plight in the world is that of a person who has had the bless-
ings we have been studying, but has lost them before gaining that final vic-
tory. This is not necessary. Only by holding confidence in God to the end can
we go to Heaven. If a saved person draws back from God, he is lost. We can
hold confidence by faithfully enduring trials, and God will turn them to good
for us. We can hold confidence by standing on God's Word, praying in the
Spirit, and keeping in the love of God. God has never lost a soul committed
to Him.
MEMORY VERSE: For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the
beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end.
—Hebrews 3:14
Danger of Falling
Hebrews 3:12-14 Take heed, brethren—give most earnest attention.
The devil is always watching for a break in a saint's armor. A little neglect
of prayer, a little giving in to some temptation, and he will insert some un-
belief to break one's trust in God.
Exhort one another—we owe duties to each other. We are members one
of another (1 Corinthians 12:25-26). A word of encouragement or prayer
may be just what a brother or sister needs to hold true. Contrary to modern
religious teachings, man can fall from the grace of God. The Scriptures in
our lesson today prove this teaching to be false doctrine. One can fall away.
To fall away after being saved is worse than having never been saved (2 Pe-
ter 2:20-21). While it is called To day—before it is too late, before Satan
deceives and blinds him to the danger until he has him trapped and bound. He
will harden the tender heart until repentance is difficult or impossible.
As long as we are partakers of Christ and as long as we hold the begin-
ning of our confidence, this trust will remain stedfast unto the end. Re-
member how you trusted Him in the first days of your Christian life? This
trust must remain. God puts it in, but we must keep it there. To stop trusting
and serving Christ at any time is to drop out of the battle.
Confidence, the Secret of Enduring
Hebrews 10:26-38 If we sin willfully—if we will to sin, choose to sin,
to do what we know is wrong after that we have received the knowledge
of the truth—after being saved and Spirit-filled, known the truth by experi-
encing it, to then choose sin is to reject Christ, the only sacrifice for sins.
There is no other. All that remains for us is fear of the Judgment and eternal
punishment. But we need not follow this road. There is no other promise for
those who stop trusting Jesus.
The Hebrews had, by their fellowship with Paul, shared in his persecu-
tions. Joyfully, because in their hearts was assurance that in heaven they
had a better and an enduring substance. Mark 10:30; Matthew 5:12—Here
the promise, there the fulfillment. Here the temporary, there the enduring.
Here the shadow, there the substance. Cast not away . . . confidence. No
one can TAKE from us the favor of God or our place in Heaven. Jesus said,
"No man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand" (John 10:29). But
we ourselves can THROW it away, or give it over to the devil. If kept, confi-
dence will bring us a great recompense of reward.
We need patience to serve without weariness, persevere without com-
plaint, and hope without losing faith, to meet sin, frustration, opposition, dif-
ficulty, failure, disaster, and delay. But Christ will come. It may seem like
a long time, but He says, "Behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with
me" (Revelation 22:12). With patience hold on to confidence.
The just shall live by faith. The justified life is sustained by faith. One
who draws back falls into a lost state (perdition) again. Yes, a saved person
can be lost, but he need not be if he keeps faith fixed in God.
God's Keeping Power Is Sure
2 Timothy 4:6-8 Paul, chained in a Roman prison, knew that he was to
be killed. The time grew near for him to be beheaded. He was not discour-
aged or fearful because he looked back on a life of trust in God. He had
present, close communion with God.
I have fought a good fight—against sin—finished my course. God had
given him a work (Acts 9:15-16). He had finished it and obtained a passing
grade. Kept the faith—kept faithful, kept his consecration true, held the be-
ginning of his confidence stedfast unto the end (Hebrews 3:14). His treas-
ures were laid up in Heaven. Now he was going to them and to his Savior.
Henceforth—from now on, the Lord would give him a crown of righ-
teousness, the reward of a righteous, Christ-filled life. All who know Christ
look forward with joy to His coming. We each can be one of them. The same
crown is for us. This is final salvation, future bliss in Heaven. We must not
miss it. If we "endure unto the end" (Matthew 24:13), it will be ours.
No Light Matter
We treat backsliding too lightly. We must endure—continue throughout
life—to reach Heaven. We underestimate salvation if we think it to be chosen
or rejected as the clothing we wear. We underestimate Satan if we think we
are free to stray and return to God at will. Many have found to their great
sorrow that straying may be easy, but that Satan has binding chains. He
catches unawares, and the power of God is the only release. Oh friend, heed
Jesus' warning: "I say unto all, Watch" (Mark 13:37). We are saved by trust-
ing Christ. We are kept in the same way. All dependence is on Him, not on
ourselves.
JUST A THOUGHT
When it comes time to die,
make sure that all you have to do is die.
LESSON 13
THE JUDGMENT
Scripture Texts: Ecclesiastes 12:13-14; Romans 2:16; John 12:48; Matthew
16:27; Romans 2:7-11; 2 Thessalonians 1:6-10; Romans 8:19-23
As people work fervently here in this life to earn an earthly living, payday
is looked forward to with great expectation. It is the reward for our labors.
The same applies to the Christian who labors and fights for the cause of
Christ through his days appointed here in this life. Death is his reward, his
final crown of victory over Satan and the power of evil.
This is the day of all days, the day he leaves all the battles behind with
their troubles and sorrows, and goes to be with Jesus in Heaven for all
eternity—PAYDAY.
MEMORY VERSE: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is
eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
—Romans 6:23
Importance of Our Response
We have been studying how God, through Jesus Christ, has given pro-
vision for each soul to live righteously. How each of us use these basic pro-
visions determines our success or failure in this life. Our response to what
God has provided determines what our payday will bring—life everlasting in
Heaven or death in hell. We must look to the Heavenly goal as the only thing
of worth.
The Day of Judgment
Ecclesiastes 12:13-14 The Bible, both the Old and New Testaments,
clearly teaches there is to be a Judgment Day, a day when all men and wom-
en shall receive their just dues (Acts 10:42; Revelation 20:12-13). We shall
all be judged according to the Gospel of Christ. The Judge is appointed by
God, and His jurisdiction includes the whole earth (Acts 17:31). Both living
and dead are included in the Judgment. Christ is that Judge (Romans 14:10).
Romans 2:16 A standard is fixed by which we shall be judged—the stan-
dard under which each lived. No one having lived under the dispensation of
grace and truth will be judged by the Law, only those living under the Law
will be judged by the Law.
The Judgment does not determine whether or not the individual is guilty.
This fact will be fully settled at death. The man or woman dying in sin will
remain guilty forever. The fact that all receive a reward at death proves this.
The Judgment will lack investigation because to God all things are fully
known. "Every knee shall bow . . . and every tongue shall confess" (Romans
14:11) without forced acknowledgment.
John 12:48 The revealed will of God is the standard of judgment. Christ
told His hearers they would be judged by His words. Judgment will depend
on the degree of knowledge of the individual, not only on what he knows, but
on what he had an opportunity to know and neglected to learn. Some have a
more complete understanding of God's will than others, so are more respon-
sible. The standards by which men are to be judged are the same as the
standards by which sin is now imputed. The Judgment will be perfectly just.
There will be no spite, but only justice.
The Day of Reward
Matthew 16:27 The same reasons that call for a Judgment require that
the Judgment be accompanied with suitable rewards. The Bible teaches fu-
ture and final rewards for all.
Romans 2:7-11 The rewards are not received on this earth. The earth is
a place of probation, a preparation place for the eternal state. Change and
decay are evident everywhere. This earth is not a suitable place for eternal
existence. The earth will be destroyed at the Day of Judgment, so it cannot
be the eternal home of either the righteous or the wicked.
2 Thessalonians 1:6-7 Heaven is a prepared place where Christ sits at the
Father's right hand awaiting the reception of the saints. He will come for us
and take us to that place where He now is. Heaven will not be this earth
made over. Heaven is a real place to which Christ ascended and from which
He will return.
2 Thessalonians 1:8-10 The wicked will be punished in hell. As Heaven
is a prepared place, so is hell. Hell is not the grave. The grave is not a place
of punishment, but a place to which all go regardless of character. It is only
the body that enters the grave. Hell is a place and not a mere condition
(Psalm 9:17), and man, "both soul and body"(Matthew 10:28), may be sent
there. The wicked shall be in a state of conscious suffering in hell. This is
described as "weeping and gnashing of teeth" (Matthew 8:12), and a place
of unquenchable fire. The rich man in hell had all his senses.
The Nature of Rewards
Romans 8:19-23 Paul here, considering only saved people, pictured God's
children as delivered from the bondage of corruption—freed from sorrow,
pain, and death. No temptation or danger of falling will be there.
Whole creation—all people, even those which have the firstfruits of the
Spirit, groan. Waiting for the adoption . . . for the redemption of our
body—to have our flesh redeemed from sickness and death, given life with
Christ forever. "Our vile body" will "be fashioned like unto his glorious
body" (Philippians 3:21). "An inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and
that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you" (1 Peter 1:4). "And they
shall reign for ever and ever" (Revelation 22:5).
Our bodies will be in Heaven, just like Jesus' risen body. He had flesh and
bones; He could handle things; He ate; He talked; He could hear. He had all
five senses. Oh, how wonderful meeting the saints of all ages! DO NOT
MISS IT.
JUST A THOUGHT
Every person is a soldier of Jesus Christ
or an agent for the devil.
